A center crossing the white line is out. Sixty seconds without a ring-out is a draw. Playback speed changes the animation, not the result.

Different routes to a good push

A front push meets bracing. Side pushes test sideways balance; rear pushes test recovery. Mass and grip resist sliding, but a heavy beetle accelerates and turns more slowly.

Tracking, reaction speed, focus and ring tactics help find a useful angle. Pushing and wandering instincts can pull in opposite directions. Endurance matters in a long contest.

THE POCKET FIELD GUIDE

Make the beetle you imagine.

Choose, breed, discover

Click a beetle for a large view, then add it to a jar. You can also drag a tank beetle into a jar slot. Put two to four different beetles in a jar, check “Use this jar,” and breed. One jar produces 10–20 babies. Two jars split that same total; an odd extra goes randomly to either. Each baby gets two distinct parents chosen randomly inside its own jar. Two parents in a jar keep that cross exclusive. Original parents stay until you remove them.

A quiet, living tank

Beetles wander after birth. Cool & pause freezes them with a brief pretend mist; Run resumes movement. Cooling, bedding, decoration and movement do not change genes or breeding chances. There are no birds, hunger or automatic mating. The optional sumo table is a harmless pushing contest. Inherited speed changes walking pace, while strength is a fictional relative trait, not a fertility advantage.

Genes that can hide

Each beetle has two copies of every gene, arranged on seven chromosome pairs. A baby gets one gamete from each of its two actual parents. Linked copies usually travel together; a crossover can exchange sections. A dominant S suppressor hides marks. Only ss reveals them; a separate T gate limits visible patterns to one color, while tt allows two. Both hidden colors and placement genes still pass on. Two Ss Tt parents with mutation off can produce plain, one-color and two-color offspring. Small broods need not match average odds.

Eighty inherited traits

Body and pattern colors, mark size and distribution, symmetry, antenna frameworks, fine hairs, leg forms, motor speed and strength all have their own inherited copies. Frameworks can mask modifiers. The stronger expression copy selects a categorical framework or pigment recipe; numeric copies average. No antenna or color is universally better. Stable developmental variation gives each baby a fixed pattern; inspecting, cooling or resizing never rerolls it.

From tiny to extravagant

Antennae include threads, beads, bristles, clubs, sawteeth, single and double combs, fans, leaf plates, elbows, plumes and side bristles. Length, width, segments, branching, fine hair and spread vary too. These mix beetle and other insect inspirations for creative play; they are not a species identification tool. Legs keep three pairs and can show runners, sturdy walkers, shovel forelegs, large hind thighs, paddles, hooks, spines and long toes.

Keep a family

The tank holds 48 beetles. Extra babies wait in the nursery. Keep up to ten favorites in the separate top-down Keep tank, return others to the breeder tank, and select descendants for later crosses. Nothing is silently discarded. Brood rounds count crossings; lineage generation follows actual ancestry. Repeated broods of the same parents are siblings.

Save your work

The lab auto-saves locally when available. Save tank file downloads a portable copy including all genes, jar groups, names and notes. Open tank file restores it. Shared class links start a fresh tank with the same founders and permissions; they do not contain your later offspring. On shared school devices, save a file before leaving. This original model teaches inheritance and is not a claim about actual beetle genetics.

BREED FOR YOUR OWN STRATEGY

Instincts, angles & a little uncertainty.

These are invented game traits. “Ring tactics” is a problem-solving parameter, not a biological intelligence test. All measurements are continuous inherited spectra, not fixed levels. Offspring inherit and may mutate real copies; a contest does not change genes or guarantee stronger offspring.

Each match has fresh decision rolls. A recorded seed can replay the same contest. Watching the animation, changing playback speed or resizing does not change the result. This is a classroom simulation, not a cheat-proof online tournament.
